overview: Hamari Dharohar – Cultural Heritage Preservation is a sub-scheme under the Ministry of Minority Affairs aimed at preserving the rich cultural heritage of minority communities in India. It focuses on safeguarding traditions, artifacts, and historical sites of notified minority communities such as Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis, and Jains. The scheme supports documentation, conservation, and promotion of cultural expressions to ensure intergenerational transmission and national recognition of minority heritage.
objectives: Preserve and promote the cultural heritage of minority communities
Document and conserve tangible and intangible cultural assets
Support restoration of historical sites and monuments
Encourage community participation in heritage conservation
Create awareness about minority cultural contributions to national identity
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include registered societies, trusts, NGOs, and institutions working in the field of cultural heritage preservation, particularly those representing notified minority communities under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992. Organizations must have a proven track record in heritage-related activities and must not be blacklisted by any government ministry or department.
benefits: Financial assistance for conservation projects, documentation of heritage, training programs, exhibitions, and publication of cultural materials. Non-financial benefits include technical guidance, networking opportunities, and recognition for contributing to national cultural diversity.
financial_support: The scheme provides grant-in-aid for approved projects, with funding typically covering up to 90% of project costs, subject to ceiling limits. Disbursement is made in installments based on milestone achievement and submission of utilization certificates.
application_process: 1. Identify a heritage conservation project aligned with scheme objectives. 2. Prepare a detailed project proposal including objectives, budget, timeline, and expected outcomes. 3. Ensure organizational eligibility and registration on NITI Aayog Darpan portal. 4. Submit the proposal through the designated channel of the Ministry of Minority Affairs. 5. Await scrutiny and approval by the concerned division. 6. Upon approval, enter into a memorandum of understanding and receive first installment. 7. Implement the project and submit progress reports. 8. Submit final report, utilization certificate, and audited statement of expenditure for final settlement.
required_documents: Land ownership or permission documents (if applicable)
Photographs and details of the heritage site/artifact
caveats: Funding is subject to availability of budget and approval of the competent authority
Projects must not overlap with similar initiatives funded by other ministries
Beneficiaries must submit utilization certificates and audited statements within stipulated time
Failure to comply with terms may lead to blacklisting and refund of funds with interest
